brief.subject: Diesel drops 16.5 cents to $6.127; fuel-card fraud warning
brief.headline: Diesel falls to $6.127 as fuel-card fraud and roadside enforcement hit carriers
brief.dek: Diesel eases, a $760K fuel-card scam shows identity-theft risk, inspectors sideline 128 drivers, and import volumes are set to cool.
brief.lede: The U.S. average diesel price fell 16.5 cents this week to $6.127 per gallon, a welcome break for carriers paying at the pump.

sections.heading: Diesel Gives Back 16.5 Cents
bullets: $6.127 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-09.
Down 16.5 cents (2.6%) from last week, easing per-mile fuel costs on every load.
Over four weeks, diesel is down 5.2 cents, so most of the relief came in one week.

sections.heading: Stolen Identity, $760K in Fuel
bullets: $760,000+ in unpaid fuel charges stem from a scheme that allegedly impersonated a Michigan trucking company.
Eight fuel cards were used for purchases across 23 states, according to a federal indictment.
Two Georgia men face charges, a reminder for small carriers to watch for anyone opening accounts in their name.

sections.heading: Inspection Blitz Reaches Maryland, DC
bullets: 1,000+ truck inspections were run by federal and state teams in Maryland and Washington, D.C.
128 drivers were sidelined, meaning lost revenue days for any carrier caught unprepared.
Separate operations in five other states turned up hundreds of violations, so keep logs and equipment inspection-ready.

sections.heading: Imports Cooling After September Peak
bullets: Port imports peaked in September and should slow through year-end, the NRF says, signaling softer drayage and import freight.
Retailers still expect imports to stay elevated through 2026 compared with typical levels.
U.S. and China extended their tariff truce until Jan. 10, 2027, keeping trade rules steady through the holidays.

sections.heading: Driverless Trucks: Costly Now, Closer Later
bullets: $4 a mile is the 2026 cost of autonomous trucks, per a Kearney and MIT Mobility Initiative report.
That report sees cost parity with human-driven trucks around 2028, a long-term competitive factor for small carriers.
Aurora's truck production schedule slipped on supply and quality issues, though it still targets 1,000+ trucks by end of 2027.
